datasets.title: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analysis of ESR1 mutated cancers in the SCANB cohort
datasets.keywords: breast cancer, proteogenomics

detail.description: Proteogenomic study combining transcriptomic, proteomic, and phosphoproteomic profiles from a subset of the SCAN-B breast cancer cohort. ESR1-mutated tumors showed higher tumor mutational burden and increased cell proliferation pathway activity. The mTOR pathway (via MTORC1) was consistently engaged across data layers and linked to poorer prognosis. Integrated analysis produced a predictive signature for ESR1 mutation status and high recurrence risk. Includes 27 ESR1-mutant samples and 108 matched control samples.

datasets.title: Local immunosuppression of tumor-draining lymph nodes via fibroblast-monocyte axis contributes to metastasis in breast cancer
datasets.keywords: DIA, breast cancer, interstitial fluid, metastasis, secretomes

detail.description: Triple-negative breast cancer is the most aggressive breast cancer subtype. Even with neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy, responses vary and patients often relapse with metastases. Using patient samples and mouse models, the study found that immunosuppressive monocytes accumulate in draining lymph nodes, recruited by fibroblastic reticular cells. Tumor-derived endogenous TLR4 ligands reprogram these fibroblasts to attract monocytes through CCL2 and CCL7. CCR2-expressing monocytes suppress T cells via PD-L1 and iNOS. Local TLR4 inhibition combined with PD-1 blockade synergistically reduced lung metastases.

datasets.title: Breaking new ground into RAD51–BRC repeats interplay in Homologous Recombination
datasets.keywords: BRCA2, RAD51, breast cancer, crosslinking

detail.description: Examines how RAD51 binds BRCA2 through its BRC repeats, a key step in repairing DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination. Combines computational and experimental biophysics, comparing binding affinity of individual BRC repeats with their effect on RAD51 disassembly, extended to larger BRCA2 fragments. Species field lists Escherichia coli (recombinant protein expression); the SDRF lists Homo sapiens.

datasets.title: Clone-by-Clone Therapy Guidance in Luminal Breast Cancer via Spatial Proteomics and Patient-Derived Tumoroid
datasets.keywords: breast cancer, drug discovery, mass spectrometry imaging, patient-derived tumouroids, precision therapy

detail.description: Pairs spatial proteomics with patient-derived tumoroids (PDTs) to guide personalized treatment in luminal breast cancer. MALDI imaging and spatially resolved micro-proteomics were applied to FFPE tumor tissue from three patients to map clonal subpopulations and their protein profiles. Pathway analysis revealed subclone-specific vulnerabilities; proteomics-informed regimens produced lower IC50 values and greater cell death than conventional chemotherapy in PDTs. Resistance markers EDIL3, CA12, PGK1, and CapG corresponded to resistant tumor clones.

datasets.keywords: B-cell lymphocytes, blood, breast cancer

detail.description: Label-free proteomic profiling compared CD14+ monocytes from peripheral blood of breast cancer patients, benign individuals, and healthy controls. Differentially expressed proteins (SRSF1, CSTB, KRT2, KRT5, APOB, APOE, ITGA2B) appeared across cohorts; APOB, HEL-S-11, KRT5, and SRSF1 showed AUC of at least 0.6 as possible classifiers. datasets.title: GYLATL1 promotes endocrine therapy resistance in luminal A-like breast cancer and is regulated by estrogen-independent ERα signaling
datasets.keywords: DIA, GLYATL1, PRM, breast cancer, endocrine therapy resistance

detail.description: Luminal A breast cancer depends on estrogen receptor-alpha (ERalpha) signaling. Endocrine therapies target this pathway, but many late-stage patients stop responding or relapse. Focusing on aromatase inhibitors in postmenopausal patients, GLYATL1 was strongly upregulated in two endocrine therapy-resistant in vitro models; levels also rose in patients during treatment, and high expression tracked with poorer survival in luminal A patients receiving aromatase inhibitors. Silencing GLYATL1 reversed resistance. Higher GLYATL1 was linked to reduced TCA cycle activity, succinate accumulation, and histone modification changes. ER positively regulated GLYATL1 only when estrogen was absent.

datasets.title: NF1-depleted ER+ breast cancers are differentially sensitive to CDK4/6 inhibitors
datasets.keywords: CDK4, NF1, RAF, breast cancer, estrogen receptor, neurofibromin 1

detail.description: Loss of neurofibromin (NF1low) is linked to endocrine therapy resistance in about 20% of early-stage ER+/HER2-negative breast cancers. Proteogenomic profiling showed NF1low tumors have elevated CDK4/6 activity. NF1 silencing increased ER binding at CCND1, raising cyclin D1. RAF directly phosphorylates the CDK4 activation loop at T172. NF1low cells respond to fulvestrant combined with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, with durable tumor regression in ER+ NF1low patient-derived xenografts. In neoadjuvant treatment, NF1low tumors on anastrozole were markedly sensitive to added palbociclib.

datasets.title: P53 orchestrates an epigenetic program that restricts stemness and maintains differentiated luminal identity in breast cancer
datasets.keywords: ER+, Exploris 480, breast cancer, luminal breast cancer, p53, stemness

detail.description: Most breast cancers are ER-positive and treated with hormone therapy such as tamoxifen. TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in breast cancer, and its mutations are linked to weaker tamoxifen response and poorer prognosis. In breast cancer cells, p53 and ER regulate genes for chromatin modifiers, raising H3K4me3 and lowering H3K9me3; this open chromatin supports luminal identity gene transcription and tamoxifen sensitivity. When p53 control weakens, tamoxifen resistance and cancer stem cell features can emerge.

datasets.title: Function and relevance of sushi domain-containing protein 2 (SUSD2) in circulating tumor cells of metastatic estrogen receptor positive breast cancer
datasets.keywords: SUSD2, breast cancer, circulating tumor cells, estrogen receptor positive, metastasis

detail.description: ER-positive breast cancers often become resistant to therapy, leading to metastasis and circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in the bloodstream. Researchers profiled the proteome of CTC-ITB-01, a CTC line from a patient with metastatic ER-alpha-positive breast cancer, quantifying about 7,954 proteins against an MCF-7 reference. SUSD2 was highly abundant and detected in CTCs from 9 of 23 breast cancer patients by CellSearch. ENPP1 was found in CTC-ITB-01 and in CTCs from 3 patients. SUSD2 overexpression in MCF-7 increased ER-alpha and GRP78 and decreased PDCD4. Low PDCD4 correlated with reduced overall survival in luminal breast cancer (n=348, p=0.0323).
detail.lab_head: Kai Bartkowiak (contact; University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf)

datasets.title: Mitochondrial respiration is a targetable vulnerability of endocrine persistence in ER+ breast cancer
datasets.keywords: ER+, breast cancer, endocrine therapy, fulvestrant, glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration, oxidative phosphorylation

detail.description: Some ER+ breast cancers return after adjuvant endocrine therapy because a small population of endocrine-tolerant persister cells survives. Genome-wide screens identified a survival strategy in which persisters reprogram metabolism and depend on mitochondrial respiration. Proteomics showed lower glycolytic enzymes in persisters; glucose tracing revealed an energy-poor state in which oxidative phosphorylation supplies ATP. In human tumors, persisters proliferating after neoadjuvant endocrine therapy had more mitochondria. Inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation with fulvestrant caused regression of patient-derived xenografts.
detail.lab_head: Arminja Kettenbach (Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth)
